entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jima of Silla was the sixth ruler of Silla, one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, and a direct descendant of Silla's founder Hyeokgeose. As the royal title in early Silla was 'isageum', Jima is commonly referred to as Jima Isageum.




 Born into a powerful Bak family, Jima rose to power after the death of his predecessor and quickly established himself as a skilled diplomat and military leader. He strengthened Silla's alliances with neighboring tribes and expanded its borders through a series of military campaigns. Jima's reign is notable for its cultural achievements, including the development of Silla's unique writing system and the promotion of Buddhism throughout the kingdom.






 Jima's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a crucial role in shaping the course of Korean history. His successors continued to build upon his achievements, eventually leading to the eventual unification of the Three Kingdoms under the Silla dynasty.






 As a testament to Jima's enduring impact, the city of Jima in South Korea remains a popular tourist destination, attracting visitors from around the world who come to explore the ruins of the ancient Silla capital, Gyeongju.
